grades.question: For now, explain ZR 37-34 as a rule, without claiming that it applies to this property. What are its glazing percentage, measurement limits, and other transparency conditions?
grades.expected: ZR 37-34: at least50percent of applicable primary-frontage street-wall area between2ft and12ft or ground-floor ceiling whichever higher, measured from adjoining sidewalk; qualifying transparency begins no higher than2ft6in subject to transom/divider exceptions, minimum2ft width, maximum10ft uninterrupted opaque width; listed parking/loading/subway/emergency-egress exclusions and37-31 exceptions; no property application.
grades.answerText:
In the supplied NYC Zoning Resolution text through 2026-08-13, ZR 37-34 requires a ground-floor-level street wall along a primary frontage to be glazed with transparent materials, which may include show windows, transom windows, or glazed portions of doors. This describes the rule only; it does not determine whether it applies to this property. (ZR 37-34)

- **Percentage and measurement band:** Transparent materials must cover at least 50% of the street-wall surface area between 2 feet above the adjoining sidewalk and 12 feet above it—or the ground-floor ceiling height, if higher. (ZR 37-34)
- **Start height and widths:** Materials counted toward the 50% may not begin higher than 2 feet 6 inches above the sidewalk, except for transom windows and window portions separated by mullions or other structural dividers. Counted materials must be at least 2 feet wide; a portion of street wall without transparency may be no wider than 10 feet. (ZR 37-34)
- **Specified excluded portions:** The transparency requirements do not apply to portions occupied by entrances or exits to accessory off-street parking facilities and public parking garages, where permitted; entryways to required loading berths, where permitted; entryways to subway stations, as applicable; or doors accessing emergency egress stairwells and passageways. (ZR 37-34)

ZR 37-31 states that the minimum-transparency requirement does not apply to Commercial District zoning lots less than 20 feet wide, measured along the street line, if the lots existed both on March 22, 2016 and on the building-permit application date. It also states an exception for a community-facility building used exclusively for “either a school, or a house of worship, listed under Use Group III(B).” The supplied wording does not resolve whether “listed under Use Group III(B)” modifies only “house of worship” or both alternatives. These are rule qualifications, not findings about this property. (ZR 37-31; ZR 37-34)

For ZR 37-30, “primary frontage” is the portion of designated frontage along a wide street; a narrow street where a Commercial District is mapped along an entire block frontage; or another frontage specifically designated as primary by a Special Purpose District or other streetscape provision. (ZR 37-311)

grades.answerText: The supplied text does not establish that you may use the high-end sidewalk elevation as one datum for the entire 50% calculation. ZR 37-34 measures the required transparent area between 2 feet and 12 feet—or the ground-floor ceiling height, if higher—“as measured from the adjoining sidewalk,” but does not say how to select a datum where that sidewalk slopes. Your sill measurements do not resolve that interpretation. An authoritative interpretation of that phrase for a sloped frontage is needed before relying on the high-end datum.
